## I42 — SKILL.md's compaction rule fires on a session crossing a multiple of 250k tokens, a crossing the agent cannot observe while it works, so no session has ever compacted and the context has grown unbounded; the rule must fire at the loop's own step boundaries - a round recorded, an item closed, a batch of findings filed - with a harness-agnostic mechanism, and it must name the fallback for a harness with no compaction primitive: a fresh session continuing from a handoff note in the repository, because the loop's state lives in the ledger and the artefacts and not in the conversation

Status: open
Source: human

- note: sharpened: the skill's own compaction needs no human. The contract is the effect, not the command: at a step boundary the working context must shrink to the loop's state, which lives in the repo, not the conversation. The skill finds the mechanism per harness instead of assuming one - opencode: opencode api session.compact --param sessionID=$OPENCODE_SESSION_ID --data '{}' returns a compaction message with delivery steer, which runs at the next step boundary, so it cannot land mid-step; claude: --autocompact auto|tokens. Where a harness has no primitive, the skill compacts itself: it writes a handoff note into the repo - item id, phase, last round, paths - and spawns the successor session unattended (claude --bg --name X -- "$(cat note)", or opencode run), because the successor is unattended in both harnesses. A fresh session is therefore not a human-gated step, and the note is a pointer set, not a summary.

## I45 — the skill's compaction rule needs an orchestrator to avoid a regress: if a session may hand off to a successor session, the session that hands off needs its own successor, and the chain only ends where some state is durable outside every conversation. The durable state is the repository - the ledger holds the item, its rounds, its list and its notes - but the phase inside an in-flight item (which stage, which staged prompt, whether a verifier has returned) is not in the ledger, so the handoff needs a pointer set written under .backlog/ (gitignored, so it never moves the verified tree: a note at the repository root does move it, since an untracked file changes the tree and R18's clean-tree test would refuse the close). The rule must say who holds the baton, that the baton is the repo plus the note and not the conversation, and that a resident orchestrator - not a chain of peers - is what spawns successors, so there is exactly one thing whose context must be kept small.

Status: open
Source: human

- note: sharpened by measurement, three facts. First, compaction and session replacement are different operations, and only the second creates the regress: a harness that can compact lets the orchestrator keep its identity and its baton, so there is no successor to spawn and no handoff to write. opencode's primitive is opencode api session.compact --param sessionID=$OPENCODE_SESSION_ID --data '{}' (the body is required; without it the call 400s), and it returns a compaction message with delivery steer - it runs at the next step boundary, so the harness itself enforces the skill's never-mid-step rule. claude's is --autocompact. Both harnesses already auto-compact on context pressure, so the skill's deliberate step-boundary compaction is the non-emergency kind. Second, the regress, once reached, terminates because the baton is the repository and not the conversation: a successor rebuilds it with bl status and bl show <id> --json, and the item's stage is derivable from its event kinds - last of file/open/brief/checks/claims/run/round says whether the list is frozen, whether claims exist, whether a run happened, whether a round was recorded. What is NOT derivable is what lives outside the repository: the staged producer and verifier prompt drafts, which today live in a temp directory, and whether a dispatched verifier has returned. Before a handoff the supervisor must land the prompts in .backlog/ or record their paths, and land the verifier's verdicts or accept re-running the verifier from the same brief. Third, a handoff note must go under .backlog/ and nowhere else: the tree builder skips .backlog/ unconditionally, so a note there never moves the verified tree, while a note at the repository root is an untracked file that git add -A picks up, changes the tree, and would trip R18's clean-tree close - measured, both facts. One context must stay small, and it is the orchestrator's: producer and verifier are already disposable children, so the rule is that the orchestrator holds pointers and not content.
- note: cross-reference: the utility that would hold the baton across a session swap is item I46, which carries the partitioning and the graceful-handover requirements. I45 keeps the regress question and the finding that the baton must be the repository, not the conversation: a successor that cannot derive the baton from the repo is a successor that guesses.

## I46 — the skill needs a dumb watcher to own session turnover so the orchestrator session stays disposable: a small out-of-process utility polls the token consumption of the running orchestrator session, and when it crosses a threshold it asks the harness to conclude the session at its next step boundary, writes the baton under .backlog/, and spawns a successor session seeded with it - unattended, no human, no regress, because the watcher holds no conversation context to grow. Measured primitives per harness: opencode - opencode api session.list reports per-session tokens (input, output, reasoning, cache read/write) so the meter is pollable from outside, opencode api session.compact --param sessionID=$OPENCODE_SESSION_ID --data '{}' returns a compaction message with delivery steer, so the harness itself enforces the never-mid-step rule, and the experimental.hook.session_completed config hook runs a command when a session completes; claude - --autocompact auto|tokens, the SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop and PreCompact hooks, and claude --bg --name X -- "$(cat note)" spawns an unattended background session that claude agents, logs, stop and rm manage; token meter - the per-assistant-message usage in the session transcript jsonl. The baton must be the repository, not the conversation: the orchestrator writes .backlog/HANDOFF.md at each step boundary with a pointer set (item id, stage, paths of the staged prompts and the dispatched verdict), and the staged prompt drafts move under .backlog/ from the temp directory, because a successor that cannot derive the baton from the repo is a successor that guesses - and the note must live under .backlog/ and nowhere else, since the tree builder skips .backlog/ unconditionally and a note at the repository root is an untracked file that moves the verified tree and would trip R18's clean-tree close.

Status: open
Source: human

- note: three additions from the human, which widen the item. First, partitioning: several sessions run at once on this laptop, across harnesses, so every watcher instance must be bound to one (directory, worktree, session id) triple - it polls only that session, concludes only that session, and spawns only into that directory - and the binding must be seamless, so a watcher started in one worktree never concludes or replaces another worktree's session, and two watchers in different worktrees never collide over the baton file, which means the baton path is derived from the worktree, not a fixed name. Second, the handover must be graceful: the watcher asks the harness to end the session, and the harness ends it - not a kill. opencode's session.compact returns delivery steer and runs at the next step boundary, which is the graceful form there; claude's background sessions have claude stop, which stops a session and keeps its conversation, and the SessionEnd and Stop hooks are the harness-side completion points. A watcher that kills the process loses the transcript, and the transcript is where the harness's own context lives. Third, the utility may be the wrong mechanism and the item must not assume it: the alternatives are (a) lean on the harness's own auto-compaction - both harnesses have it - and change nothing, so the skill's rule becomes 'compact at the loop's step boundary' with the harness doing it, (b) make the loop end an item by ending its session, so session turnover is a property of the loop's shape rather than a watcher, and (c) the watcher. The item should settle which, and (a) is the cheapest if the skill's rule can be made harness-agnostic enough to be satisfied by each harness's own compaction. Prior art to read before deciding: /Users/simran/codebase/opencode-handoff-on-context, an opencode plugin that watches the root session's tokens, summarizes, writes .opencode-handoff/ and launches a fresh session, and /Users/simran/codebase/ctxed for cross-harness context accounting.
